source.paraphrase: A promise that is not awaited, returned, or explicitly ignored can reject with nobody handling it.

invariants.why: A floating promise rejects into an unhandled rejection. The caller continues as if the work had been scheduled with a result.
invariants.fixHint: Await the call, return the promise, or prefix it with void when the fire-and-forget is intentional.
invariants.avoid: Adding .catch that ignores the error still leaves the promise floating. void is the explicit discard. fetch without an Async name is a timeout rule in the vibe-proof pack, not this one.

relations.why: TRPC-ERR-001 tells procedures to throw a TRPCError, and TS-THROW-001 denies every throw inside an exported function; routers are exported, so following one fix violates the other.
relations.settle: Exclude router files from TS-THROW-001 (for example **/routers/** or **/server/api/**): tRPC turns a thrown TRPCError into the typed failure the client branches on.

relations.why: SK-FORM-001 tells form actions to throw error() for unexpected failures, and TS-THROW-001 denies that throw inside the exported actions object.
relations.settle: On SvelteKit 2 call error(...) without the throw keyword: it throws itself and no throw statement remains. On SvelteKit 1, exclude **/+page.server.ts and **/+server.ts from TS-THROW-001.

relations.why: SK-ERROR-001 tells load functions to throw error(500, ...) with a static message, and TS-THROW-001 denies that throw inside the exported load.
relations.settle: On SvelteKit 2 call error(...) without the throw keyword: it throws itself and no throw statement remains. On SvelteKit 1, exclude the **/+page.server.ts, **/+layout.server.ts and **/+server.ts route files from TS-THROW-001.

relations.why: NEST-CODE-001 directs error responses to a thrown HttpException, and TS-THROW-001 denies throws inside methods of an exported controller class.
relations.settle: Exclude **/*.controller.ts from TS-THROW-001: Nest maps a thrown HttpException to the response. Keep TS-THROW-001 on services and domain code.

source.locator: return a result instead of throwing across a boundary
source.paraphrase: Expected failures are values. Reserve throw for defects. An exported function lists its failures in its return type.

invariants.why: A throw on the exported boundary forces every caller into try/catch and loses the typed failure the caller could have handled.
invariants.fixHint: Return a result object such as { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, error } and let the caller branch.
invariants.avoid: Throwing from an exported arrow is the same boundary. A private function that is not inside the export may throw; the export should translate that into a result.
